messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT OPENED: Datadog ingestion delay detected in us-west-2 (metrics + logs ingestion lagging). Alert volume spiking. Please acknowledge. https://status.datadoghq.com/incident/xyz123

jamal: taking this. paging oncall (PD) now. I'll post initial findings here. :eyes:

mika: seeing no new datapoints for several high-cardinality metrics (api.requests, api.latency) since ~16:12 UTC. Traces also stalled — sampling shows last spans at 16:11. Logs appear delayed by ~10-15m.

alex: support-bot just reported customer-facing errors (spike in 502/504) for webhook delivery. Not sure if related but time aligns. customers: several mid-market tenants with high throughput.

jamal: quick checks running — agent health, pipeline backpressure, and any local disk pressure. attaching commands I ran:```bash
# check agent / pipeline
sudo systemctl status datadog-agent
dd-agent status | grep -i ingest
# sample output we saw:
ingest_lag: 1200s
no new metrics since 2024-03-15T16:12:05Z
```

mika: confirmed ingest_lag metric on our side too. Host-level agents are up; connectors to datadog seem healthy locally but the ingestion window is stale. Could be DD-side ingestion or the aggregator.

jamal: immediate mitigation plan: 1) mute noisy/data-quality alerts to reduce paging storm 2) switch critical alerting to backup alert path (Prometheus -> Alertmanager) for uptime signals 3) open support case with Datadog and request a dedicated bridge + ETA 4) enable agent-side buffered forwarding and start persisting raw logs to S3 for last 24h in case we need post-mortem. Doing steps 1 and 2 now.

mika: done with muting non-actionable alerts (dashboard: infra->alerts). I created a temporary Alertmanager route to catch CPU/502/latency signals and escalate to phones. Patch ID: temp-route-20240315.

support-bot: Customer impact update: support queue shows ~18 tickets tied to webhook failures since 16:15 UTC. Triage: medium-high severity for three enterprise customers. I notified account reps and posted a short message to customers in impacted cohort.

jamal: opened support ticket with Datadog (INC-98765) and requested bridge. Pasted ingestion diagnostics and agent outputs. Contacted our Datadog AM (cc'd). Link: https://support.datadoghq.com/ticket/INC-98765

mika: note — because Datadog ingestion is delayed, our normal dashboards and traces are unreliable. That means blind spots: we can't see recent error patterns or reliably attribute which service is root cause. We should rely on local metrics, host logs persisted to S3, and customer-reported symptoms until DD confirms restore.

alex: For customer comms: recommend we tell customers we have degraded observability due to a third-party ingestion issue and are actively mitigating. Avoid giving spurious root-cause until we have traces.

jamal: rolling a temporary playbook entry into the incident doc: "Third-party observability outage — use backup telemetry + persist raw logs + reduce alert noise + open vendor bridge." Copying snippet:```
- When vendor ingestion lag detected:
  - Mute non-actionable vendor alerts
  - Switch critical uptime alerts to backup pipeline
  - Start log export to durable storage (S3)
  - Open vendor support case + request bridge and ETA
  - Inform support + AMs for customer comms
```

sophie: I'm oncoming in 25m. Handoff notes: ingestion lag ongoing, Datadog investigating, support tickets rising, mitigation steps in place (muted alerts + Alertmanager failover). Please leave the ticket link and AM contact in the incident doc. I'll take over ownership when my shift starts. @jamal can you post any changes in the next 20m I should know about? :coffee:

jamal: will do. current status: waiting on DD bridge. no ETA from support yet. account manager pinged. temporary Alertmanager routes active. archived snapshot of dashboards pushed to S3 for investigation.

datadog-bot: Status update from Datadog: "We are experiencing delayed ingestion for a subset of customers in us-west-2. Our engineering team is investigating. No ETA at this time." (link: https://status.datadoghq.com/incidents/xyz123)

mika: small note on detection: add a synthetic that queries our backup Prometheus every 1m to detect these vendor-blindspot situations in future. We should alert on divergence between vendor metrics and our local metrics.

jamal: agreed. I'll file a follow-up infra ticket to add the synthetic and the runbook entry. Ticket: INF-4051.

datadog-bot: 30m later update: "Ingestion pipeline partially recovered in us-west-2; backlog being processed. Some metrics/logs may appear delayed up to 45 minutes. Continued monitoring."

mika: I'm starting to see some datapoints trickle in — api.latency has samples at 16:52 UTC. Not full recovery yet.

support-bot: customers updated: we posted a status note to impacted customers and will follow up when Datadog confirms full restoration. No new major escalations.

sophie: I am in. Handoff: ingestion partly recovered but monitor for full catch-up for at least 10 minutes. Priorities: keep alerts muted until we confirm backlog processed, keep support comms steady, escalate to AM if no full recovery in 30m. Taking over incident ownership.

jamal: handing off to @sophie. I'll remain available for questions. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

datadog-bot: RESOLVED: "Ingestion pipeline restored in us-west-2. Backlog processed. We are monitoring for anomalies."

mika: verification: metrics continuous for 12 minutes, traces flowing, logs ingestion caught up for most hosts. Marking observability as restored from our side. We'll keep the incident open for postmortem and runbook updates.

sophie: closing actions: 1) document the blind-spot mitigation steps and add synthetic divergence alert 2) post-mortem to include timeline and customer impact 3) follow up with Datadog AM for RCA and SLA credit request. I'll create the postmortem stub in #postmortems.

jamal: thanks everyone. Incident status: mitigated -> in recovery -> postmortem pending.

incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated, owner=@sophie, incident_id=INC-20240315-01
